Lines on Mapbox

Source: vignettes/articles/r-docs/lines-on-mapbox.Rmd
lines-on-mapbox.Rmd

Map Tiles

plotly.core bundles plotly.js 4, where the Mapbox-based traces were replaced by MapLibre-based “map” traces. The "open-street-map" and carto-* styles need no access token. See Map Layers for more information.

Lines on tile maps using “Scattermap” traces

To draw a line on your map, you either can use add_scattermap() (see go_scattermap()) or add_scattergeo() (see go_scattergeo()) in plotly.core. This example uses scattermap and sets the drawing mode to the combination of markers and lines.

library(plotly.core)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_scattermap(
    mode = "markers+lines",
    lon = c(10, 20, 30),
    lat = c(10, 20, 30),
    marker = go_scattermap_marker(size = 10)
  ) |>
  add_scattermap(
    mode = "markers+lines",
    lon = c(-50, -60, 40),
    lat = c(30, 10, -20),
    marker = go_scattermap_marker(size = 10)
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    map = go_map(
      style = "open-street-map",
      center = go_map_center(lon = 10, lat = 10),
      zoom = 1
    ),
    margin = go_margin(l = 0, t = 0, b = 0, r = 0)
  )

fig

#Reference

See go_scattermap() for more information and options!
